text:
maya: heads up — saw a handful of rows in the console insights that look like they're from a different org. noticed after the staging rollout at ~09:12 UTC. :eyes:
raj: repro steps? can you paste the query or link?
maya: quick link: https://console.internal/redwood/insights?snap=last24h — filter by project id 21 and you'll see two rows with org_id: 88 showing up under org 21. only happens when i switch tabs fast.
tina: hmm, session-mux changes went in this morning (PR #7894). suspects: header affinity + prefetch cache TTL tweaks.
luis: pinging the router team — did we change any header normalization? we removed the X-Org-Id fallback last week but added a prefetched org hint.
ops-bot: deploy v2.14.3 to console-router completed at 2026-03-18T09:10:23Z (hash: b7c9f1a).
raj: maya can you run curl against the internal preview api and include the headers you see when it flashes? maybe the org header is getting dropped on the handoff. e.g.:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Console-Org: 21" \
  "https://internal-api/preview?panel=insights&project=21"
```
maya: here's the raw-ish capture — sometimes `X-Console-Org` is present, othertimes it's `X-Org-Hint: 88` and there's no X-Console-Org.
raj: that smells like a race in the prefetch middleware that can rewrite headers when a stale cache entry returns. i remember a guard was relaxed to reduce latency.
tina: PR notes from #7894 mention "avoid blocking prefetch on auth token fetch" — that could let a prefetched response attach the wrong org hint if the new auth token arrives after prefetch completes.
luis: if the prefetch attaches org hints to responses and then we reuse that response across sessions, we get cross-org leakage. we should treat prefetched payloads as org-agnostic unless we canonicalize header bind at the final render step.
maya: we only see it on rapid tab switches, not on single page reloads. repro: 1) open org 21, 2) switch to org 88 quickly, 3) switch back to org 21. sometimes the ghost rows remain for ~30s.
raj: can we add a quick canary: drop prefetched org headers unless token matches current session token? cheap guard to test hypothesis.
tina: i can push a revert for the relaxed guard and add a log to prefetch that prints `prefetch.bound_org` and `session.org` for mismatch counts. low-risk revert?
luis: prefer a feature-flagged mitigation to avoid rollback across all customers. add `PREFETCH_STRICT_BIND=true` to the console-router config for canary subset.
ops-bot: feature flag `prefetch-strict-bind` created and enabled for 5% of traffic at 2026-03-18T10:05:00Z.
maya: added screenshots and a short Loom to the ticket: https://loom.internal/vid/abc123 — shows the ghost rows flicker.
raj: good. next steps: (1) enable strict bind on staging (tina) (2) add logs for prefetch header binding (tina) (3) run simulated rapid-switch load test to confirm (raj) (4) monitor telemetry: cross_org_row_count and prefetch_mismatch_rate (luis).
tina: i'll push the staging flag now and follow up with logs. i have a small patch that sets `X-Console-Org` at render time if mismatch detected.
luis: also add quota sanity check: ensure prefetch cache keys include org_id as a top-level key — accidental omission could have widened cache reuse.
maya: thanks — will stand by to validate on staging. if we can patch fast we can avoid a customer-facing incident. :pray:
raj: label this P1 until we confirm it's isolated to prefetch. update thread when staging results are in.
ops-bot: alert: cross_org_row_count exceeded threshold (10) for org 21 at 2026-03-18T10:12:08Z — triggered paging to eng-platform on-call.
maya: i'm on-call pickup, will follow up in 15.
raj: logging note: make sure telemetry doesn't attribute leaked rows to the wrong org metrics; we need separate telemetry field `leaked_from_org` for postmortem.
tina: agreed. creating short follow-up doc in the ticket with data model change suggestion.
luis: if this is confirmed, we'll schedule a controlled rollout of the strict bind across regions next week.
maya: updating ticket now with repro steps + logs. thanks all.
